neighbours.label: The slot just before a war-zone country is named (' in', ' of' or ' and' after talk of foreign military action, heading to Syria, Iraq or Afghanistan); soldiers in peaceful countries stay quiet
fire: The senator condemned the American airstrikes in Syria during a long speech.
Britain cut its last combat troops in Afghanistan that autumn.
Critics blamed the prolonged occupation of Iraq for the rise in oil prices.
The Kremlin defended its bombing campaign in Syria on state television.
Many veterans of the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan still struggle to find work.
Human rights groups documented war crimes in Syria and Yemen last year.
The president ordered a military surge in Afghanistan shortly after taking office.
Reporters covered the insurgency in Iraq from a hotel in the capital.
quiet: The senator praised the American airbases in Germany during a long speech.
Britain cut its last combat troops in Belize that autumn.
Critics blamed the prolonged drought in Spain for the rise in oil prices.
The Kremlin defended its gas pipeline in Germany on state television.
Many veterans of the navy in Canada and Norway still struggle to find work.
Human rights groups opened new offices in Norway and Denmark last year.
The president ordered a trade review in Japan shortly after taking office.
Reporters covered the elections in Austria from a hotel in the capital.

notes: Card: ' in' x18 before Syria, Iraq, Afghanistan; ' and' and commas inside such lists; the + pole reads the same way for Morocco.
